## Installation

First install [`ir`](https://r-lib.github.io/ir/#installation), which runs R
scripts and installs the packages they need. Then install `rush` as an `ir`
tool, which puts a `rush` command on your `PATH`:

```sh
ir tool install github::jeroenjanssens/rush
```

Check that it works:

```{term}
rush --version
```

That's it; there's no R package to load. The first time a command needs a
package (say, ggplot2 for a plot), `ir` installs it for you.

To upgrade `rush` later, install it again. `--force` replaces the installed
command, and `--refresh` makes `ir` look up the latest version:

```sh
ir tool install --force --refresh github::jeroenjanssens/rush
```

## Quick tour

Evaluate an R expression. Its value is printed:

```{term}
rush run '6 * 7'
```

Give `rush run` a file, and it is read into a data frame called `df` before
your expression runs. Here, we first save R's `mtcars` data set as CSV:

```{term}
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
rush run 'head(df, 5)' mtcars.csv
```

In the terminal, the result is printed as a table. When you pipe it into
another command, `rush` writes CSV, so you can keep going, including with
another `rush`. Use `-` to read from standard input:

```{term}
rush run 'head(df, 10)' mtcars.csv |
  rush run 'dplyr::select(df, mpg, cyl, hp)' -
```

Data without a header row works too. With `-H`, the columns are named `x1`,
`x2`, and so on:

```{term}
seq 6 | rush run -H '2 * sum(df$x1)' -
```

Load packages with `-l`, or the whole tidyverse with `-t`, to use their
functions without the `package::` prefix:

```{term}
rush run -t 'count(df, cyl, sort = TRUE)' mtcars.csv
```

Query files directly with SQL:

```{term}
rush sql "SELECT cyl, ROUND(AVG(mpg), 1) AS avg_mpg, COUNT(*) AS n
          FROM mtcars GROUP BY cyl ORDER BY avg_mpg DESC" mtcars.csv
```

Convert between formats:

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.parquet mtcars.csv
rush run 'nrow(df)' mtcars.parquet
```

Draw a plot in the terminal:

```{term}
rush plot -x wt -y mpg -c 'factor(cyl)' mtcars.csv
```

Every command writes a small R script and runs it. Use `--dry-run` (`-n`) to
see that script, and save it to build on:

```{term}
rush run -n 'dplyr::filter(df, mpg > 25)' mtcars.csv
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv mtcars.parquet
```
